item.text:
**Verdict:** No.

2023 evidence points to continued executive dominance over courts, parliament, local government, and oversight bodies. I found only weak counterevidence: formal complaint channels and limited reactive discipline in a few cases. None of that shows Putin strengthening independent institutions when they constrained him.

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Short claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Russia: Freedom in the World 2023 Country Report | Freedom House | 2023 | [link](https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2023) | Freedom House says the judiciary lacks independence, judges’ careers depend on Kremlin preferences, and the 2020 constitutional amendments strengthened presidential control over the legislature and courts. It also says the system uses a controlled media environment and a subservient judiciary, which is the opposite of strengthening independent oversight. | 4B.4, 4B.2, 4B.3 |
| Russia: Nations in Transit 2023 Country Report | Freedom House | 2023 | [link](https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/nations-transit/2023) | Freedom House says Russian governance is dominated by repression and that local autonomy had already been effectively eliminated, with wartime centralization tightening executive control further. It also says municipal councils retained only narrow, pressured space, which is not evidence of a ruler strengthening local governments. | 4B.4, 4B.2, 4B.3 |
| Russia: 2023 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices | U.S. Department of State | 22 Apr 2024 | [link](https://www.state.gov/reports/2023-country-reports-on-human-rights-practices/russia) | The report says authorities often denied independent investigations, impunity remained the norm for police and prison officials, and oversight bodies were weak and fear retaliation. That directly cuts against any claim that Putin strengthened institutions that could constrain him. | 4B.4, 3B.4, 3B.8 |
| Доклад о деятельности Уполномоченного по правам человека в Российской Федерации за 2023 год | Russian Human Rights Commissioner, via Garanti | 2023 | [link](https://base.garant.ru/409190604/) | This is the main weak counterexample: the ombudsperson says 36 torture/coercion complaints were registered and 33 were upheld, with two police officers facing criminal cases. It shows limited reactive complaint handling, not meaningful independent institutional strengthening. | 4B.4, 3B.4 |
| Ministry of Justice of the Russian Federation FAQ on complaints and appeals | Ministry of Justice of the Russian Federation | 2023 | [link](https://minjust.gov.ru/ru/appeals/faq/589/) | The ministry says citizens can report crimes, investigators must register and review complaints, and complainants can appeal. This is formal due-process architecture, but it is not evidence that Putin strengthened independent courts or oversight bodies in practice. | 4B.4, 3B.4 |
| Russia: Nations in Transit 2024 Country Report | Freedom House | 2024 | [link](https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/nations-transit/2024) | Looking back at 2023, Freedom House says local autonomy had eroded, electoral integrity worsened, and the remaining municipal space was shrinking and tightly controlled. Its one limited counterpoint is that municipal councils still served as a thin opposition training ground, but that is residual space, not institutional strengthening. | 4B.4, 4B.2, 4B.3 |

**Search gap:** I did not find credible 2023 evidence that Putin strengthened independent courts, legislatures, audit bodies, local governments, or oversight institutions in a way that empowered them to constrain him. The available evidence runs the other direction, with only formal procedures and limited reactive complaint handling as weak counterexamples.
